'''''Viola kitaibeliana''''', the '''dwarf violet''', is a plant species in the genus [[Viola (plant)|''Viola'']]. It is native to a large area from the Canary Islands, across Europe, to northern Iran and southern Turkmenistan.<ref name=PoWO/>

It is an [[Annual plant|annual]], and requires disturbed or grazed soil to grow.<ref name="Barkham">{{cite news |last1=Barkham |first1=Patrick |title=Dwarf pansy blooms on tiny Scilly island after 16-year absence |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/may/29/dwarf-pansy-blooms-on-isles-of-scilly-after-16-year-absence |access-date=29 May 2021 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=2021-05-29 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, two plants were discovered flowering on the 0.16 sq km island of [[Teän]], in the [[Scilly Isles]]; the first seen there for 16 years.<ref name="Barkham" />

==Taxonomy==
Besides the [[Nominate (taxonomy)|nominate]] taxon, there are two other infraspecific taxa which are recognised in [[Plants of the World Online]] as of 2017:<ref name=PoWO/>
*''Viola kitaibeliana'' subsp. ''kitaibeliana''
*''Viola kitaibeliana'' subsp. ''machadiana'' <small>(Cout.) Capelo & C.Aguiar</small>
*''Viola kitaibeliana'' subsp. ''trimestris'' <small>(DC. ex Ging.) Espeut</small>

==Description==
This [[herbaceous plant]] is not higher than 12 cm. Like all violets the flowers are [[Floral symmetry|zygomorphic]].
